answer: Identity should rest on a measured hardware pulse, not key files. Each module records the drift of its quartz timing reference across a long challenge and photographs the pigment flecks in the resin sealing its ferrous shield; both become its record. Each epoch the node answers a latency challenge checked against that drift and a camera re-verifies the seal. Cloning a key onto many hosts leaves one shared drift, so clones collide and are refused. Extra identities cost a module and seal, and probing the resin to read the key disturbs the pigment, voiding it. Cost scales in units, not addresses.
